title: Where Light Dies
narration: A shadow against a glowing ring. That is M87*. Its event horizon spans 19 billion kilometers. Our entire solar system could fit behind it. This is where space ends.
visual_goal: Start on the iconic 2019 orange-ringed black hole image, then zoom in to show the dark void swallowing a stylized solar system for scale.

title: The Invisible Giant
narration: Einstein predicted this in 1915. But we couldn't see one until 2019. Then, in 2022, we focused on our own center. Sagittarius A*. Four million suns in a space smaller than a star.
visual_goal: Show a sepia-toned photo of Einstein, then flash-forward to the 2022 blurry image of Sgr A* pulsing over a Milky Way backdrop.
search_queries: solar system vs black hole size

title: A Collision in Time
narration: The first image is a still life. But black holes move. In 2015, LIGO heard a collision. Two holes, 36 and 29 suns, spiraled and merged. Space itself rang.
visual_goal: Show an animated gravitational wave ripple distorting a starfield, followed by two abstract dark objects spiraling into each other in a 90s anime style.

title: The Eraser
narration: They erase the past. No hair, no scars. Only mass, charge, spin. But Hawking asked: does the universe remember? His 1974 radiation says the black hole forgets. Information is lost.
visual_goal: A paper sketch of a featureless sphere wiping away complex equations, then a ghost-like Hawking concept image with musical notes evaporating from a black hole.

title: The Final Page
narration: The paradox remains. No answer yet. M87* is 55 million light-years away. The secrets are deep. But we have their picture. The ending? We are still writing it.
visual_goal: Return to the first M87* image, but slowly fade to a blank starry sky, suggesting an unfinished page or a waiting horizon.
